settingsd

The headless native ABP desktop settings authority, contract 1.0.0. An established profile has one writer and durable whole-document settings and operation receipts. Native publication is retained and owner-stamped by noded. Ced and compd's scene-host consume shared appearance jobs on their existing Bus lifetimes. Full desktop integration, panel geometry and native frame acceptance remain in development.

See the settings contract. Clients use the settings library. The source is services/settingsd.

Running it

settingsd init --instance example
settingsd seed --allow-create --instance example
settingsd serve --instance example

Init explicitly initialises new state. An installer can explicitly seed a first-run session profile with --allow-create. Plain seed validates an existing profile unchanged and refuses a wholly missing root; a retained writer lock prevents seed from recreating an established missing primary, including without a backup. Serve fails for a missing or unsupported established store. Both accept --profile and --root for an explicit binding or test directory. Use an isolated broker when testing.

Topics and mirrors

Contract 1.0.0 publishes one retained topic per settings prefix, settingsd.desktop.keys.<profile>.<prefix> (appearance, window, shell.panels, time and so on, 22 in all), plus the follower view settingsd.desktop.look.<profile> and the schema 3 snapshot settingsd.desktop.snapshot.<profile>. A prefix body carries every key under it with its defaults filled, the resolved mode and accent beside the authored choice for appearance, and changed_at, the revision that last changed it. A commit republishes only the topics whose content moved; a broker reconnect republishes all of them. Live keys (network, Bluetooth, system, audio levels) are in no topic: their owners publish them.

Retained topics are node-local, so a machine has one authority and every desk on it runs a mirror:

settingsd serve --instance alpha                     # the authority
settingsd serve --instance alpha --mirror-of alpha   # a desk's mirror

A mirror attaches with settings.mirror.attach, keeps the authority's record in a sealed cache, and republishes the same topics on its own node from each settings.mirror.revision push. It answers reads from the cache, forwards writes and relays the authority's receipts, and refuses writes as authority_unreachable while the authority is down; settings.status then reports stale: true. Nothing polls: the authority pushes each revision (with a bounded retry, dropping a mirror that keeps failing), a mirror re-attaches when its own broker reconnects, and a restarted authority pushes to the mirrors it had attached (mirrors.json beside the store is a hint: an entry that fails its first push is dropped).

The mirror commands keep their integrity checks on the open Bus. A push or stop notice is taken only from the configured authority's settingsd as the broker stamps the sender (broker_peer, broker_service), an attach only from the node it names, at most 16 mirrors attach, and a mirror never takes an older incarnation of the record.

One gap is known: a crashed authority sends no notice, and noded has no peer-down event a service can hear (topics are node-local and the mesh link state is internal). A mirror then reports current until its next forwarded write is refused, which marks it stale; the same holds when the authority's broker goes away. Only a clean stop is seen at once.

settings.source {binding, digest} answers the pinned design source when digest is the profile's current source_digest, and stale_digest with the current one otherwise (theming ADR R14a).

Profiles and upgrades

Profiles pin their initial package design source. Reload checks a content digest; a binary upgrade cannot change effective settings within the same revision. An effective interpretation digest fences compiler drift for explicit migration. The accepted record's format (store::FORMAT, now 4) is that migration: an older record whose seal verifies as stored is re-derived and re-sealed on open by Accepted::upgrade, whose doc comment says how to add the next field.

Format 4 re-derives the renamed Workshop app context. After verifying the stored seal, it drops any retired apps.busviewer override with a warning, advances the profile revision when dropping authored settings, and atomically re-seals both the primary and any valid backup. Other app overrides, the pinned design source and receipt history are preserved.

An embedded default can outlive the compiler rules that accepted it. If an accepted desktop has no authored appearance.source, fails resolution, and its pinned source digest exactly matches a known retired package default, the upgrade re-pins it to this binary's embedded default. It keeps authored appearance choices, advances both profile and design revisions, retains receipts, and atomically re-seals each valid primary and backup. The retired embedded tokens disappear with the old package source; there is no separate authored token override map. A failing authored source or unknown embedded source still refuses with the compiler's token/rule diagnostics, without rewriting the store. Valid older sources stay pinned.

The known defaults are the earlier installed source from 740c0c13 (33a33291c676de5bd1c30cb395534e8656244f57e6771a98bd61e3669e11f235) and v0.1.2 at fe9dfa90, last changed by bc2faa69 (34726165cf21927a700a0eb8e5770f6a374d44a7cc2f2fc09d987faf2a288ce2). As of 2026-10-24, published release history contains only v0.1.2; v0.1.1 is an unpublished draft and there is no v0.1.0 tag. No other shipped default is inferred from unreleased source edits. Init continues to pin the actual source so accepted revisions remain reproducible; following the running binary by reference would change settings without a revision or receipt fence.

Present corrupt primary data can restore a validated backup under a new incarnation. A missing primary fails visibly, including when a backup exists. I/O faults and intact unsupported documents fail without automatic rollback.

The unit

The packaged unit binds the instance to its machine hostname; its session/VT number is a supervision attribute and never a second instance identity. The session target wants and upholds the authority. The unit validates with plain seed before serving, and application and compositor startup does not wait for settings readiness. An image must provision its service account's writable MIXOS_ETC/settings root and explicitly seed once during first installation. Automatic startup never receives --allow-create, so lost mounts or directories do not silently become new default profiles.

Tests

Worker tests: cargo test -p settingsd. The broker tests (tests/bus.rs: change-only topics on one broker, then an authority and a mirror on a private broker pair) run with MIXOS_TEST_NODED naming a noded built from the same commit and --ignored. The compositor fixtures arrive with the desktop test harness.
